title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
titleEn: The Tale of the Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
part: Night 36 · The Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 296–301 (Night 36, continuing directly from nights-35), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 36 continues the tale of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and Anīs al-Jalīs. The ship carries the lovers toward Baghdad while the sultan's mamluks smash their empty house and the vizier al-Muʿīn is reassured; in Baghdad Nūr al-Dīn and the slave-girl fall asleep at the gate of the garden called Bustān al-Nuzha, which belongs to the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd. The old keeper, Shaykh Ibrāhīm, is about to beat them, thinks better of it, and welcomes them in; Nūr al-Dīn tricks the scrupulous old man into fetching wine, and the girl coaxes him into drinking with them as the dawn ends the night. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā-kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when-the-night-came-to-be, the night, the sixth and the thirty,
sentences.i: When the thirty-sixth night came,
sentences.n: The print joins فلماكانت into one word, and, as on the previous nights, has الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; both are kept as printed, with the dagger alif marking the missing long ā.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الرَّئِيسَ لَمَّا قَالَ لِعَلِيٍّ نُورِالدِّينِ إِلَى دَارِ السَّلَامِ مَدِينَةِ بَغْدَادَ فَطَلَعَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَطَلَعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ مَعَهُ وَعَوَّمُوا وَأَرْخَوُا الْقُلُوعَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-raʾīsa lammā qāla li-ʿAliyyin Nūri al-Dīni ilā dāri al-salāmi madīnati Baghdāda fa-ṭalaʿa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-ṭalaʿati al-jāriyatu maʿahu wa-ʿawwamū wa-arkhawu al-qulūʿa
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that the captain, when he said to ʿAlī Nūr al-Dīn: to the abode-of-peace, the city of Baghdad — then went-up Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, and went-up the slave-girl with him, and they set-afloat and loosed the sails.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the captain had spoken to ʿAlī Nūr al-Dīn of their course to the Abode of Peace, the city of Baghdad, Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī went aboard, and the girl went aboard with him; and the crew pushed off and let out the sails.
sentences.n: The speaker is Shahrazād, and the captain (الرئيس) is the master of the ship on which the pair have embarked. The captain's words to ʿAlī read as if some of them have dropped out: لما قال … إلى دار السلام has no verb of motion or speech to carry the destination, so I translate only what is printed and supply "of their course" in the idiomatic layer. The print has a full stop after الجارية and carries on with معه on the next line; the sentence is one, and the stop is not reproduced. طلع ("go up") is the usual word for going aboard. عوموا is a colloquial form, probably "they set (her) afloat, pushed off"; the subject is the crew, unnamed. دار السلام, "the Abode of Peace", is a standing name of Baghdad.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتِ الْمَرْكَبُ كَأَنَّهَا طَيْرٌ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا بَعْضُهُمْ وَأَحْسَنَ شِعْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajati al-markabu ka-annahā ṭayrun bi-janāḥayhi kamā qāla fīhā baʿḍuhum wa-aḥsana shiʿra
sentences.l: And went-out the ship as-if-it (were) a bird with its-two-wings, as said about-it some-of-them, and did-well (in) poetry:
sentences.i: And the ship sped forth like a bird upon its wings, even as one of them said of her, and said it well in verse:
sentences.n: Here markab is treated as feminine (خرجت), as is common for ships. The print has شعر without a final alif; I vocalise it as a bare accusative, شِعْرَ, "(he did well) in verse", since there is no alif to carry a tanwīn. The line leads straight into the verse that follows. The print gives كأنها with a precomposed hamza, which is kept.

sentences.t:
اُنْظُرْ اِلَى مَرْكَبٍ يُسْبِيكَ مَنْظَرُهُ * تُسَابِقُ الرِّيحَ فِي سَيْرٍ وَمَجْرَاءِ
كَانَّهُ طَائِرٌ قَدْ مَدَّ اَجْنِحَةً * اَتَى مِنَ الْجَوِّ مُنْقَضًّا عَلَى الْمَاءِ
sentences.tr:
unẓur ilā markabin yusbīka manẓaruhu * tusābiqu al-rīḥa fī sayrin wa-majrāʾi
ka-annahu ṭāʾirun qad madda ajniḥatan * atā mina al-jawwi munqaḍḍan ʿalā al-māʾi
sentences.l:
Look at a ship — captivates-you its sight — * she outstrips the wind in going and in running,
as-if-it (were) a bird that has stretched wings, * come from the air, swooping upon the water.
sentences.i: Behold a ship whose very sight enchants you, * outracing the wind in her course and her running; like a bird with outspread wings * that has come down from the air, swooping upon the water.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print; every word is marked there, so nothing is added. يُسْبِيكَ is printed with damma on the first letter, where Classical would have يَسْبِيكَ; I leave it as printed. مَجْرَاءِ is printed with a hamza, for majrā, which also gives the rhyme in -āʾi. تُسَابِقُ is feminine, agreeing with the ship.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَسَارَتْ بِهِمُ الْمَرْكَبُ وَطَابَ لَهُمُ الرِّيحُ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-sārat bi-himu al-markabu wa-ṭāba lahumu al-rīḥu
sentences.l: He said: And went the ship with them, and was-pleasant to-them the wind.
sentences.i: So the ship sailed on with them, and the wind blew fair for them.
sentences.n: قال here is the narrator's "she said" carried over from the opening; Shahrazād speaks throughout. بهم and لهم take a final u before the following al-.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاجَرَى لِهَؤُلَاءِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā-jarā li-hāʾulāʾi
sentences.l: This (is) what-happened to these.
sentences.i: So much for these;
sentences.n: The print joins ماجرى into one word. هؤلاء has its hamza printed on a wāw-seat, so it is kept precomposed. This unit ends the slice: it is the first half of the storyteller's turning formula, which continues into the next slice ("and as for …"), so the sentence may not be complete here.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاجَرَى لِلْمَمَالِيكِ فَإِنَّهُمْ جَاؤُا عَلَى بَيْتِ الْوَزِيرِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ فَكَسَرُوا الْأَبْوَابَ وَدَخَلُوا وَطَافُوا الْأَمَاكِنَ فَلَمْ يَفْعُوا لَهُمَا عَلَى خَبَرٍ فَهَدَمُوا الدَّارَ وَرَجَعُوا وَأَعْلَمُوا السُّلْطَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā jarā li-al-mamālīki fa-innahum jāʾū ʿalā bayti al-wazīri Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin fa-kasarū al-abwāba wa-dakhalū wa-ṭāfū al-amākina fa-lam yafʿū lahumā ʿalā khabarin fa-hadamū al-dāra wa-rajaʿū wa-aʿlamū al-sulṭāna
sentences.l: And as-for what happened to-the-mamluks: they came upon the house of-the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, and broke the doors and entered and went-round the places, and did not light, for the-two-of-them, upon any news; and demolished the house, and returned, and informed the sultan.
sentences.i: As for what befell the mamluks, they came to the house of the vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, broke down the doors, entered, and searched every corner, but found no news of the pair. So they pulled the house down, went back, and informed the sultan.
sentences.n: ماجرى is printed as one word. جاؤا is the print's spelling of جاؤوا, “they came”. يفعوا is evidently a printing slip for يقعوا (yaqaʿū): وقع على خبر is “to light upon news of”, and the ف is printed where ق belongs; I vocalise the letters as they stand and read the sense “find”. The mamluks are the sultan's slave-soldiers, sent to arrest the pair.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السُّلْطَانُ اُطْلُبُوهُمَا مِنْ أَيِّ مَكَانٍ كَانَا فِيهِ فَقَالُوا السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sulṭānu uṭlubūhumā min ayyi makānin kānā fīhi fa-qālū al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: And the sultan said: Seek-them-two from whatever place the-two were in it. And they said: The hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: The sultan said, “Seek them out, from whatever place they may be in.” And they answered, “With hearing and obedience.”
sentences.n: The print has السمع والطاعة without the بـ of the usual reply بالسمع والطاعة; I vocalise it as a bare phrase, “[ours is] hearing and obedience”, which means the same.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوِى إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَكَانَ خَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ السُّلْطَانُ خِلْعَةً وَاطْمَأَنَّ قَلْبُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma nazala al-wazīru al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī ilā baytihi wa-kāna khalaʿa ʿalayhi al-sulṭānu khilʿatan wa-iṭmaʾanna qalbuhu
sentences.l: Then went-down the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī to his house, and the sultan had bestowed upon him a robe-of-honour, and his heart grew-tranquil.
sentences.i: Then the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī went down to his house. The sultan had bestowed a robe of honour upon him, and his heart was at ease.
sentences.n: وكان خلع is a pluperfect (“had bestowed”): the robe was given before he left. The print has بن without the initial alif of ابن, as is usual between a first name and a father's name; I read it as ibn.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ مَا يَأْخُذُ بِشَارَكَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَدَعَى لَهُ بِطُولِ الْعُمْرِ وَالْبَقَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu al-sulṭānu mā yaʾkhudhu bishāraka illā anā fa-daʿā lahu bi-ṭūli al-ʿumri wa-al-baqāʾi
sentences.l: And the sultan said to him: Not takes your-glad-tidings(-gift) except I; and he prayed for him with length of-the-life and the continuance.
sentences.i: The sultan said to him, “None but I shall take your bishāra.” And the vizier called down blessings on him: long life and lasting days.
sentences.n: بشارك is printed without the tā' of بشارتك (or it stands for بشراك); a bishāra is the gift paid to the bearer of good news. The clause is obscure: the sultan probably means that he alone will reward the vizier. I give it as it stands. دعى is the print's spelling of دعا, “he prayed”; the one praying is the vizier, for the sultan.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ أَمَرَ أَنْ يُنَادِيَ فِى الْمَدِينَةِ يَا مَعَاشِرَ النَّاسِ كَافَّةً قَدْ أَمَرَ مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانُ أَنَّ مَنْ عَثَرَ بِعِلْمِي نُورِالدِّينِ ابْنِ خَاقَانَ وَجَاءَ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ خَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ خِلْعَةً وَأَعْطَاهُ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَمَنْ أَخْفَاهُ أَوْعَرَفَ مَكَانَهُ وَلَمْ يُخْبِرْ بِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْتَحِقُّ مَا يَجْرِي لَهُ مِنَ النَّكَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-sulṭāna amara an yunādiya fī al-madīnati yā maʿāshira al-nāsi kāffatan qad amara mawlānā al-sulṭānu anna man ʿathara bi-ʿilmī Nūri al-Dīni ibni Khāqāna wa-jāʾa bihi ilā al-sulṭāni khalaʿa ʿalayhi khilʿatan wa-aʿṭāhu alfa dīnārin wa-man akhfāhu aw ʿarafa makānahu wa-lam yukhbir bihi fa-innahu yastaḥiqqu mā yajrī lahu mina al-nakāli
sentences.l: Then indeed the sultan commanded that one-cry in the city: O company-of the people, all-together: Our lord the sultan has commanded that whoever stumbles, by-my-knowledge, upon Nūr al-Dīn son-of Khāqān and comes with him to the sultan, he bestows upon him a robe-of-honour and gives him a thousand dinars; and whoever hides him, or knows his place and does not inform about him, then indeed he deserves what runs for-him of the exemplary-punishment.
sentences.i: Then the sultan commanded that a crier proclaim through the city: “O people, one and all! Our lord the sultan has decreed that whoever chances upon word of Nūr al-Dīn ibn Khāqān and brings him to the sultan shall receive a robe of honour and a thousand dinars; but whoever hides him, or learns where he is and does not report it, shall deserve the punishment that will befall him.”
sentences.n: The print has بعلمي, “by my knowledge”, which does not fit a proclamation in the sultan's own third person; it is probably a slip for بعلم, “with knowledge of”. I vocalise it as printed and translate “chances upon word of”. أوعرف is printed as one word, أو عرف, “or knows”. The decree is a conditional with no particle: من عثر … خلع عليه, “whoever finds … [the sultan] bestows on him”. نكال is punishment meant to deter, an example made of the culprit.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ الطَّلَبُ عَلَى نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ فَمَا وُجِدَ لَهُ حِسْنٌ وَلَا خَبَرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa al-ṭalabu ʿalā Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin fa-mā wujida lahu ḥisnun wa-lā khabarun
sentences.l: And the search fell upon Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, and there was not found of him a trace, nor news.
sentences.i: So the hunt for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī began, but not a trace nor a word of him was to be found.
sentences.n: The print has حسن, which I read as حِسّ, “trace, sound”, the second half of the set phrase حسّ ولا خبر, “neither sign nor tidings”; the final ن looks like a stray letter or a spelled-out tanwīn. I vocalise the letters as they stand.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ هَؤُلَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā mā kāna min amri hāʾulāʾi
sentences.l: And this (is) what was of the affair of these.
sentences.i: So much for them.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ نُورِالدِّينِ وَجَارِيَتِهِ فَإِنَّهُمَا وَصَلَا بِالسَّلَامَةِ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri Nūri al-Dīni wa-jāriyatihi fa-innahumā waṣalā bi-al-salāmati ilā Baghdāda
sentences.l: And as-for what was of the affair of Nūr al-Dīn and his slave-girl: indeed the-two arrived in safety at Baghdad.
sentences.i: As for Nūr al-Dīn and his slave-girl, they reached Baghdad in safety.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الرَّئِيسُ هَذِهِ بَغْدَادُ وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ أَمِينَةٌ قَدْ وَلَّى عَنْهَا الشِّتَاءُ بِبَرْدِهِ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا فَصْلُ الرَّبِيعِ بِوَرْدِهِ وَأَزْهَرَتْ أَشْجَارُهَا وَجَرَتْ أَنْهَارُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-raʾīsu hādhihi Baghdādu wa-hiya madīnatun amīnatun qad wallā ʿanhā al-shitāʾu bi-bardihi wa-aqbala ʿalayhā faṣlu al-rabīʿi bi-wardihi wa-azharat ashjāruhā wa-jarat anhāruhā
sentences.l: And the captain said: This (is) Baghdad, and it (is) a city secure; winter has turned away from it with its cold, and the season of-the-spring has advanced upon it with its roses, and its trees have flowered and its rivers have flowed.
sentences.i: The captain said, “This is Baghdad, a city of safety. Winter with its cold has departed from it, and the season of spring with its roses has come upon it; its trees are in flower and its rivers run.”
sentences.n: The captain's speech is in rhymed prose (sajʿ): بِبَرْدِهِ / بِوَرْدِهِ, then أَشْجَارُهَا / أَنْهَارُهَا, which the literal layer follows (“with its cold … with its roses”). الرئيس is the ship's captain.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ طَلَعَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَجَارِيَتُهُ مِنَ الْمَرْكَبِ وَأَعْطَى لِلرَّئِيسِ خَمْسَةَ دَنَانِيرَ وَطَلَعَا مِنَ الْمَرْكَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ṭalaʿa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-jāriyatuhu mina al-markabi wa-aʿṭā li-al-raʾīsi khamsata danānīra wa-ṭalaʿā mina al-markabi
sentences.l: And at that, went-up Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and his slave-girl from the ship, and he gave to the captain five dinars, and the-two went-up from the ship.
sentences.i: Thereupon Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and his slave-girl came ashore; he gave the captain five dinars, and the two of them climbed out of the ship.
sentences.n: طلع (“go up”) is the usual word for leaving a boat for the bank. The print says “left the ship” twice, once before and once after the payment; both are translated.

sentences.t: وَسَارَا قَلِيلًا فَرَمَتْهُمَا الْمَقَادِيرُ بَيْنَ الْبَسَاتِينِ فَجَاءَا إِلَى مَكَانٍ فَوَجَدَاهُ مَكْنُوسًا مَرْشُوشًا بِمَسَاطِبَ طُولَانِيَّةٍ وَقَوَادِيسَ مُعَلَّقَةٍ مَلَانَةٍ بِالْمَاءِ وَفَوْقَهُ مُكَعَّبٌ مِنَ الْقَصَبِ بِطُولِ الزُّقَاقِ وَفِي صَدْرِ الزُّقَاقِ بَابُ بُسْتَانٍ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ مَغْلُوقٌ
sentences.tr: wa-sārā qalīlan fa-ramathumā al-maqādīru bayna al-basātīni fa-jāʾā ilā makānin fa-wajadāhu maknūsan marshūshan bi-masāṭiba ṭūlāniyyatin wa-qawādīsa muʿallaqatin malānatin bi-al-māʾi wa-fawqahu mukaʿʿabun mina al-qaṣabi bi-ṭūli al-zuqāqi wa-fī ṣadri al-zuqāqi bābu bustānin illā annahu maghlūqun
sentences.l: And the-two walked a-little, and the fates cast-them between the gardens, and the-two came to a place and found-it swept, sprinkled, with benches long and water-jars hanging, full with-the-water; and above it a lattice of-the-cane along the length of-the-lane, and at the head of-the-lane the door of-a-garden — save that it (was) bolted.
sentences.i: They walked on a little way, and Fate cast them down among the gardens. They came to a spot which they found swept and sprinkled, with long benches and hanging jars full of water; above it a trellis of cane ran the length of the lane, and at the head of the lane stood the door of a garden, though it was shut fast.
sentences.n: قواديس (sing. قادوس) are here water-jars hung up for passers-by to drink from. مكعب من القصب is obscure; I take it as cane-work in a lattice, a trellis shading the lane. ملانة is the colloquial form of ممتلئة, “full”, and مغلوق the colloquial passive of غلق, “shut, bolted” (Classical مغلق). المقادير, “the decrees, the fates”, is the plural of قدر.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِىٌّ لِلْجَارِيَةِ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا مَحَلٌّ مَلِيحٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun li-al-jāriyati wa-Allāhi inna hādhā maḥallun malīḥun
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to-the-slave-girl: By-God, indeed this (is) a place pretty.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to the girl, “By God, this is a charming spot.”
sentences.n: Here the print spells ʿAlī with final ى (على) rather than ي; I keep the letter as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَاسَيِّدِي اِقْعُدْ بِنَا سَاعَةً عَلَى هَذِهِ الْمَسَاطِبِ نَأْخُذْ لَنَا رَاحَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yāsayyidī iqʿud binā sāʿatan ʿalā hādhihi al-masāṭibi naʾkhudh lanā rāḥatan
sentences.l: And she said: O-my-master, sit with-us an-hour on these benches; let-us-take for-us a rest.
sentences.i: She said, “My lord, let us sit awhile on these benches and take some rest.”
sentences.n: يَاسَيِّدِي is printed as one word. نأخذ follows the command directly, with no particle, in the sense “so that we may take”; I vocalise it as a jussive, the Classical form for that pattern.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعَا وَجَلَسَا عَلَى الْمَسَاطِبِ ثُمَّ غَسَلَا وُجُوهَهُمَا وَأَيْدِيَهُمَا وَضَرَبَهُمَا الْهَوَاءُ فَنَامَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿā wa-jalasā ʿalā al-masāṭibi thumma ghasalā wujūhahumā wa-aydiyahumā wa-ḍarabahumā al-hawāʾu fa-nāmā
sentences.l: And the-two went-up and sat on the benches, then washed their-two faces and their-two hands, and the air struck-them, and the-two slept.
sentences.i: So they climbed up and sat on the benches, washed their faces and hands, and the breeze played over them, and they fell asleep.

sentences.t: جَلَّ مَنْ لَا يَنَامُ
sentences.tr: jalla man lā yanāmu
sentences.l: Exalted is he who does-not sleep.
sentences.i: Exalted is He who never sleeps.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on جلّ, which I keep. It is a pious aside: only God never sleeps, unlike the two who have just dropped off. I write “He” because the phrase is a formula for God.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هَذَا الْبُسْتَانُ يُسَمَّى بُسْتَانَ النُّزْهَةِ وَفِيهِ قَصْرٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ قَصْرُ الْفُرْجَةِ وَالتَّمَاثِيلِ وَهُوَ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ هَارُونَ الرَّشِيدِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hādhā al-bustānu yusammā bustāna al-nuzhati wa-fīhi qaṣrun yuqālu lahu qaṣru al-furjati wa-al-tamāthīli wa-huwa li-al-khalīfati Hārūna al-Rashīdi
sentences.l: And this garden was called the-garden of-the-Delight, and in it (was) a palace, it-is-said to-it the-palace of-the-Spectacle and-the-Images, and it (was) belonging-to the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd.
sentences.i: Now this garden was called the Garden of Delight, and in it stood a palace known as the Palace of the Spectacle and the Statues, which belonged to the Caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd.
sentences.n: الفرجة is a spectacle or entertainment, and التماثيل are images, statues or figures; the name is “the Palace of the Spectacle and the Images”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْخَلِيفَةُ إِذَا ضَاقَ صَدْرُهُ يَأْتِي إِلَى هَذَا الْبُسْتَانِ وَالْقَصْرِ وَيَقْعُدُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-khalīfatu idhā ḍāqa ṣadruhu yaʾtī ilā hādhā al-bustāni wa-al-qaṣri wa-yaqʿudu fīhi
sentences.l: And the caliph, whenever his chest grew-narrow, would come to this garden and the palace and sit in it.
sentences.i: Whenever the Caliph felt his spirit oppressed, he would come to this garden and its palace and sit there.
sentences.n: ضاق صدره, “his chest grew narrow”, is the idiom for being oppressed and out of sorts; its opposite, انشرح صدره, “his chest opened”, comes two units on. كان + present marks a habit.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْقَصْرُ لَهُ ثَمَانُونَ شُبَّاكًا وَمُعَلَّقٌ فِيهَا ثَمَانُونَ قِنْدِيلًا وَفِي وَسَطِهِ شَمْعَدَانٌ كَبِيرٌ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-qaṣru lahu thamānūna shubbākan wa-muʿallaqun fīhā thamānūna qindīlan wa-fī wasaṭihi shamʿadānun kabīrun mina al-dhahabi
sentences.l: And the palace had to-it eighty windows, and hanging in-it (were) eighty lamps, and in its middle a candelabrum, large, of gold.
sentences.i: The palace had eighty windows, with eighty lamps hung in them, and in its midst a great candelabrum of gold.
sentences.n: The print marks شُبَّاكا (damma, shadda) and I keep those marks. ثمانون is nominative where Classical would put a different case after كان له; the print is kept as it stands. The pronoun in فيها is feminine singular, “in it”, referring to the plural windows (or to the palace's hall).

sentences.t: فَإِذَا دَخَلَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَمَرَ الْجَوَارِيَ أَنْ تَفْتَحَ الشَّبَابِيكَ وَأَمَرَ بِإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ النَّدِيمِ وَالْجَوَارِي أَنْ يُغَنُّوا فَيَنْشَرِحَ صَدْرُهُ وَيَزُولَ هَمُّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā dakhalahu al-khalīfatu amara al-jawāriya an taftaḥa al-shabābīka wa-amara bi-Isḥāqa ibni Ibrāhīma al-nadīmi wa-al-jawārī an yughannū fa-yanshariḥa ṣadruhu wa-yazūla hammuhu
sentences.l: And when the caliph entered it, he ordered the girls that she-open the windows, and ordered (the bringing of) Isḥāq son-of Ibrāhīm the boon-companion and the girls that they-sing, so that his chest opened and his care vanished.
sentences.i: Whenever the Caliph entered it, he would bid the girls open the windows, and would send for Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm the boon-companion, and for the girls, to sing; and so his heart was eased and his cares fell away.
sentences.n: أمر بـ, “command (the bringing of)”, takes the person sent for. The verb تفتح is singular though the girls are many, and يغنوا is masculine plural for a mixed company; both are common in this text. The past tense after إذا is iterative, “whenever”. انشرح صدره, “his chest opened”, is the opposite of ضاق صدره above.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لِلْبُسْتَانِ خَوْلِيٌّ شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna li-al-bustāni khawliyyun shaykhun kabīrun yuqālu lahu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu
sentences.l: And there was to-the-garden a gardener, an-elder, large (in years), it-is-said to-him the-Shaykh Ibrāhīm.
sentences.i: The garden had a keeper, a very old man, who was called Shaykh Ibrāhīm.
sentences.n: خولي is the keeper or gardener of an estate; شيخ كبير is a man of great age.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ إِذَا خَرَجَ يَقْضِي حَاجَتَهُ يَجِدُ الْمُتَفَرِّجِينَ مُعَلِّمَ الْقَصَّابِ فَيَغْضَبُ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna idhā kharaja yaqḍī ḥājatahu yajidu al-mutafarrijīna muʿallima al-qaṣṣābi fa-yaghḍabu ghaḍaban shadīdan
sentences.l: And he, whenever he went-out to-fulfil his need, would find the spectators, the master of-the-butcher, and become-angry an-anger severe.
sentences.i: And whenever he went out to answer a call of nature, he would come upon the sightseers, the butcher's master among them, and fly into a violent rage.
sentences.n: معلم القصاب, “the butcher's master”, stands in the print with no connecting word after المتفرجين; it may be a second group of loiterers or may be corrupt (a word may have dropped out). I translate what is there and add “among them” only to make the English run. قضاء الحاجة, “fulfilling a need”, is the polite idiom for relieving oneself; the loungers gather at the gate and obstruct him.

sentences.t: فَصَبَرَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ حَتَّى جَاءَ عِنْدَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabara al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu ḥattā jāʾa ʿindahu al-khalīfatu fī baʿḍi al-ayyāmi fa-aʿlamahu bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And the Shaykh Ibrāhīm was-patient until came to-him the caliph on some of-the-days, and he informed him of that.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm bore it patiently until the Caliph came to him one day, and he told him of it.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on الايّام, which I keep.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ أَيُّ مَنْ أَصَبْتَهُ عَلَى بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ افْعَلْ مَعَهُ مَا أَرَدْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu ayyu man aṣabtahu ʿalā bābi al-bustāni ifʿal maʿahu mā aradta
sentences.l: And the caliph said: Whichever one you find at the door of-the-garden, do with him what you wished.
sentences.i: The Caliph said, “Whomever you find at the garden gate, do with him as you please.”
sentences.n: أيّ من is “whoever”, with the resumptive pronoun in أصبته, “you find him”; ما أردت, literally “what you wanted”, is “whatever you like”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ خَرَجَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْخَوْلِيُّ لِقَضَاءِ حَاجَةٍ عَرَضَتْ لَهُ فَوَجَدَ الِاثْنَيْنِ نَائِمَيْنِ عَلَى بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ مُغَطِّيَيْنِ بِإِزَارٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna dhālika al-yawmu kharaja al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu al-khawliyyu li-qaḍāʾi ḥājatin ʿaraḍat lahu fa-wajada al-ithnayni nāʾimayni ʿalā bābi al-bustāni mughaṭṭiyayni bi-izārin wāḥidin
sentences.l: And when it was that day, the Shaykh Ibrāhīm the gardener went-out for the fulfilling of a need that presented to-him, and found the two sleeping at the door of-the-garden, covering-themselves with a wrapper, one.
sentences.i: When that day came, Shaykh Ibrāhīm the keeper went out on a need that had arisen, and found the two of them asleep at the garden gate, covered with a single sheet.
sentences.n: مغطيين is printed for the passive dual مغطّيين, “covered”, with the final letters as in a genitive/accusative dual; it is vocalised as printed. إزار is a wrap or cloth that can be used as a sheet.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ هَؤُلَاءِ مَا عَرَفَا أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ أَعْطَانِي إِذْنٌ وَمَرْسُومٌ أَنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ لَقِيتُهُ هُنَا أَقْتُلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun hāʾulāʾi mā ʿarafā anna al-khalīfata aʿṭānī idhnun wa-marsūmun anna kulla man laqītuhu hunā aqtuluhu
sentences.l: And he said: By-God, good! These, not they-two knew that the caliph gave me a permission and a decree: that every one whom I-meet here, I-kill him.
sentences.i: He said, “By God, splendid! These two did not know that the Caliph has given me leave and a decree that I may kill anyone I meet here.
sentences.n: هؤلاء ما عرفا pairs a plural “these” with a dual verb, and اذن ومرسوم stands as a bare pair of nouns after the verb of giving, in the nominative; the print has no case endings here and I vocalise as it stands. The speech continues in the next unit; the quotation mark is left open.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَنَا أَضْرِبُ هَذَيْنِ ضَرْبًا شَنِيعًا حَتَّى لَا يَتَقَرَّبَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ بَابِ الْبُسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin anā aḍribu hadhayni ḍarban shanīʿan ḥattā lā yataqarraba aḥadun min bābi al-bustāni
sentences.l: But I strike these-two a-striking hideous, until not approach anyone from the door of-the-garden.
sentences.i: But I shall give these two a fearful beating, so that no one will dare come near the door of the garden.”
sentences.n: This unit continues the gardener's speech begun in the previous unit (“…and decree … but …”). The printed sentence may run on past this point. حتى لا يتقرب, “so that he not approach”, takes the subjunctive.

sentences.t: وَقَطَعَ جَرِيدَةً خَضْرَاءَ وَخَرَجَ إِلَى عِنْدِهِمَا وَشَالَ يَدَهُ حَتَّى بَانَ عَنْ بَيَاضِ إِبْطِهِ وَأَرَادَ ضَرْبَهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-qaṭaʿa jarīdatan khaḍrāʾa wa-kharaja ilā ʿindihimā wa-shāla yadahu ḥattā bāna ʿan bayāḍi ibṭihi wa-arāda ḍarbahumā
sentences.l: And he cut a frond, a green one, and went out to at-them-two, and lifted his hand until it showed, away from the whiteness of his armpit, and wanted the striking-of-them-two.
sentences.i: He cut a green palm-rod and went out to where the two lay, and raised his hand until the whiteness of his armpit showed, meaning to beat them.
sentences.n: The slice opens in the middle of a sentence, so this is a fragment: the man who does all this (the old garden-keeper, Ibrāhīm) is named only in the next unit. جريدة is a palm frond stripped of its leaves, used as a switch; شال is the colloquial “to lift, raise”; إلى عندهما, “to at them”, is a Middle Arabic way of saying “to where they were”.

sentences.t: فَتَفَكَّرَ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَقَالَ يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ كَيْفَ تَضْرِبُهُمَا وَلَمْ تَعْرِفْ حَالَهُمَا وَقَدْ يَكُونَانِ غَرِيبَيْنِ أَوْ مِنْ أَبْنَاءِ السَّبِيلِ وَرَمَتْهُمَا الْمَقَادِيرُ هُنَافَأَنَا أَكْشِفُ وُجُوهَهُمَا وَأَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-tafakkara fī nafsihi wa-qāla yā Ibrāhīmu kayfa taḍribuhumā wa-lam taʿrif ḥālahumā wa-qad yakūnāni gharībayni aw min abnāʾi al-sabīli wa-ramathumā al-maqādīru hunā fa-anā akshifu wujūhahumā wa-anẓuru ilayhimā
sentences.l: And he reflected in his self and said: O Ibrāhīm, how do-you-strike-them-two, and you-have-not known their-state? And perhaps they-two-are two-strangers or from the sons-of the road, and the fates have-cast-them-two here. So I, I-uncover their-two faces and look at-them-two.
sentences.i: Then he reflected within himself and said, “Ibrāhīm, how can you strike them when you do not know who they are? They may well be strangers, or wayfarers whom the fates have cast up here. Let me uncover their faces and look at them.”
sentences.n: The old man talks himself out of the beating. أبناء السبيل, “sons of the road”, means travellers. The print runs هنا and فأنا together as one word, هنافانا; it is kept as one token. فأنا أكشف is “so I will uncover”, a plain present of intent.

sentences.t: فَشَالَ الْإِزَارَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمَا وَقَالَ هَذَانِ حَسَنَانِ لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ أَضْرِبَهُمَا فَغَطَّى وُجُوهَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-shāla al-izāra ʿan wujūhihimā wa-qāla hādhāni ḥasanāni lā yanbaghī an aḍribahumā fa-ghaṭṭā wujūhahumā
sentences.l: And he lifted the wrapper from their-two faces and said: These two (are) two fair-ones; not is-it-fitting that I strike-them-two. And he covered their-two faces.
sentences.i: He lifted the cloth from their faces and said, “These two are comely; it is not fitting that I should beat them.” And he covered their faces again.
sentences.n: الإزار is the wrapper or sheet the sleepers had drawn over their faces. حسنان is the dual of حسن, “fair, good-looking”.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَ لِرِجْلِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ وَجَعَلَ يَكْبِسُهَا فَفَتَحَ عَيْنَهُ فَوَجَدَ عِنْدَ رِجْلَيْهِ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا عَلَيْهِ هَيْبَةٌ وَوَقَارٌ
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddama li-rijli Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin wa-jaʿala yakbisuhā fa-fataḥa ʿaynahu fa-wajada ʿinda rijlayhi shaykhan kabīran ʿalayhi haybatun wa-waqārun
sentences.l: And he stepped forward to the foot of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and began to knead-it, and he opened his eye and found, at his two feet, a shaykh, great, upon him (being) awe and dignity.
sentences.i: Then he stepped up to Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī's foot and began to massage it; and Nūr al-Dīn opened his eyes and found at his feet a venerable old man, of awe-inspiring and dignified bearing.
sentences.n: The print has the singular رجل (“foot”) here, and the pronoun in يكبسها is feminine singular to match; two words on, عند رجليه has the dual. كبس is “to press, knead”, the shampooing-massage a servant gives a sleeper's feet as a courtesy. نورالدين is printed as one word and kept so; the first ففتح عينه has Nūr al-Dīn as its subject.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَحَى نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَلَمْ رِجْلَيْهِ وَقَعَدَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ وَأَخَذَيَدَ الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَبَاسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-istaḥā Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-lam rijlayhi wa-qaʿada ʿalā ḥaylihi wa-akhadhayada al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma wa-bāsahā
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī was-ashamed, and not his-two-feet, and sat on his strength, and took the hand-of the shaykh Ibrāhīm and kissed it.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī was abashed, and [...] his feet; he pulled himself upright, took Shaykh Ibrāhīm's hand and kissed it.
sentences.n: The print has ولم at the end of one line and رجليه at the start of the next, with no verb between: a word or more has evidently dropped out (perhaps “did not let go of”, perhaps “did not leave”), and I do not guess, so the literal layer shows the gap and the idiomatic layer marks it with [...]. واخذيد is printed as one word, “and-took-hand-of”. على حيله is “on his own strength”, that is, sitting up unaided; حيل (Classical حَيْل, strength) is the colloquial form. باسها, “kissed it”, uses the colloquial باس for the Classical قبّل; the pronoun is feminine because يد is.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي أَنْتَ مِنْ أَيْنَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu lahu yā waladī anta min ayna
sentences.l: And the shaykh said to him: O my son, you (are) from where?
sentences.i: The old man said to him, “My son, where are you from?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي نَحْنُ غُرَبَاءُ وَفَٰرَتِ الدَّمْعَةُ مِنْ عَيْنَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī naḥnu ghurabāʾu wa-fārati al-damʿatu min ʿaynayhi
sentences.l: And he said: O my master, we (are) strangers; and the tear welled from his two eyes.
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, we are strangers.” And a tear welled from his eyes.
sentences.n: The speaker is Nūr al-Dīn. The print has وفرت, which I read as وفارت, “welled up”, with the dagger alif supplying the missing long ā; it could conceivably be a form of فرّ, “fled”, but “a tear welled” is what the sense wants.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَا وَلَدِي اِعْلَمْ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَوْصَى عَلَى إِكْرَامِ الْغَرِيبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu yā waladī iʿlam anna al-nabiyya ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama awṣā ʿalā ikrāmi al-gharībi
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: O my son, know that the Prophet — God prayed upon him and greeted — enjoined upon the honouring-of the stranger.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm said, “My son, know that the Prophet, God bless him and give him peace, enjoined the honouring of the stranger.”
sentences.n: صلى الله عليه وسلم is the blessing always said after the Prophet's name. أوصى على, “enjoined upon”, uses على where Classical would say أوصى بـ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي مَا تَقُومُ تَعْبُرُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَتَتَفَرَّجُ فِيهِ وَيَنْشَرِحُ صَدْرُكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu yā waladī mā taqūmu taʿburu ilā al-bustāni wa-tatafarraju fīhi wa-yanshariḥu ṣadruka
sentences.l: Then he said to him: O my son, not you-rise, you-cross to the garden, and you-stroll in it, and expands your-breast?
sentences.i: Then he said to him, “My son, why not get up and come across into the garden, and stroll about in it, and let your heart be eased?”
sentences.n: ما تقوم تعبر is a spoken invitation: ما here means “why not?”, and the two verbs stand side by side with no أن (“why don't you rise (and) cross”). ينشرح صدرك, “your breast expands”, means that your heart is eased and cheered.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ يَاسَيِّدِي هَذَا الْبُسْتَانُ لِمَنْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni yāsayyidī hādhā al-bustānu li-man
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said to him: O-my-master, this garden, to whom?
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said to him, “Sir, whose garden is this?”
sentences.n: نورالدين and ياسيدي are each printed as one word and kept so. هذا البستان لمن, “this garden — to whom?”, is the ordinary way to ask “whose?”.

sentences.t: قَالَ يَا وَلَدِي هَذَا الْبُسْتَانُ وَرِثْتُهُ مِنْ أَهْلِي
sentences.tr: qāla yā waladī hādhā al-bustānu warithtuhu min ahlī
sentences.l: He said: O my son, this garden, I-inherited-it from my family.
sentences.i: He answered, “My son, this garden I inherited from my people.”

sentences.t: وَمَا كَانَ قَصْدُ الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بِهَذَا الْكَلَامِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَطْمَئِنَّا وَيَعْبُرَا الْبُسْتَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā kāna qaṣdu al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma bi-hādhā al-kalāmi illā an yaṭmaʾinnā wa-yaʿburā al-bustāna
sentences.l: And not was the intent of-the-shaykh Ibrāhīm by this speech except that they-two be-at-ease and cross the garden.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm meant nothing by these words but that the two should be put at ease and come into the garden.
sentences.n: This unit ends the slice and the sentence may run on into the next one. يطمئنا is printed with ئ (a precomposed character), which is kept; the dual subjunctive يطمئنّا, “that they two be at ease”, has no final nūn after أن.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ كَلَامَهُ شَكَرَهُ وَقَامَ هُوَ وَجَارِيَتُهُ وَالشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ قُدَّ امَهُمَا فَدَخَلُوا الْبُسْتَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni kalāmahu shakarahu wa-qāma huwa wa-jāriyatuhu wa-al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu qudd āmahumā fa-dakhalū al-bustāna
sentences.l: And when Nūr al-Dīn heard his speech, he thanked him, and rose, he and his slave-girl and the shaykh Ibrāhīm, in-front-of-them-two; and they entered the garden.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard his words, he thanked him and rose, he and his slave-girl, with Shaykh Ibrāhīm going before them; and they entered the garden.
sentences.n: The print splits قدامهما into قد and امهما (“in front of them both”); I point the two halves as printed and they are read together as quddāmahumā. نورالدين is printed as one word and kept so.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا هُوَ بُسْتَانٌ وَأَيُّ بُسْتَانٍ بَابُهُ مُقَنْطَرٌ كَأَنَّهُ إِيوَانٌ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā huwa bustānun wa-ayyu bustānin bābuhu muqanṭarun ka-annahu īwānun
sentences.l: And behold, it (was) a garden — and what (a) garden! — its door vaulted, as-if-it a vaulted-hall.
sentences.i: And behold, it was a garden — and what a garden! Its gateway was arched, like the great vaulted hall of a palace.
sentences.n: وأيّ بستان is the exclamatory “and what a garden!”; the print puts a shadda on the yā' and it is kept. The إيوان is a large vaulted hall open on one side.

sentences.t: عَلَيْهِ كُرُومٌ وَأَعْنَابُهُ مُخْتَلِفَةُ الْأَلْوَانِ
sentences.tr: ʿalayhi kurūmun wa-aʿnābuhu mukhtalifatu al-alwāni
sentences.l: Over it (were) vines, and its grapes (were) varied-of colours:
sentences.i: Vines grew over it, and its grapes were of many colours:

sentences.t: الْأَحْمَرُ كَأَنَّهُ يَا قُوتٌ وَالْأَسْوَدُ كَأَنَّهُ آبَنُوسٌ
sentences.tr: al-aḥmaru ka-annahu yā qūtun wa-al-aswadu ka-annahu ābanūsun
sentences.l: the red (one), as-if-it a ruby, and the black (one), as-if-it ebony.
sentences.i: the red like rubies, and the black like ebony.
sentences.n: The print writes ياقوت (“ruby”) as two words, يا قوت; I keep the split and point them as one word read together. آبنوس is printed with the madd sign and is kept so.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلُوا تَحْتَ عَرِيشَةٍ فَوَجَدُوا فِيهَا الْأَثْمَارَ صِنْوَانًا وَغَيْرَ صِنْوَانٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalū taḥta ʿarīshatin fa-wajadū fīhā al-athmāra ṣinwānan wa-ghayra ṣinwānin
sentences.l: And they entered beneath a trellis, and found in it the fruits, twin-rooted and not twin-rooted.
sentences.i: Then they went in beneath an arbour, and found in it fruits growing from joined roots and from single roots alike.
sentences.n: صنوان وغير صنوان is borrowed from the Qur'an (13:4), where it describes date-palms that share one root and palms that each have their own; here it is applied to the fruit-trees.

sentences.t: وَالْأَطْيَارُ عَلَي الْأَغْصَانِ تُغَرِّدُ بِالْأَلْحَانِ وَالْهَزَارُ يُرَجِّعُ الْأَفْنَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-aṭyāru ʿalā al-aghṣāni tugharridu bi-al-alḥāni wa-al-hazāru yurajjiʿu al-afnāna
sentences.l: And the birds upon the branches warble with the melodies, and the nightingale trills the varieties.
sentences.i: The birds upon the branches warbled their melodies, and the nightingale trilled its many strains.
sentences.n: علي is the print's spelling of على (a dotless-looking yā' for alif maqṣūra, common in Middle Arabic); it is pointed as ʿalā. الافنان can be “the boughs” or “the varieties, kinds”; since the verb is يرجّع, “to trill, repeat a tune”, I read “varieties (of song)”, and it is a loose phrase either way. The lines are in rhymed prose, with the rhyme on -ān.

sentences.t: وَالْقُمْرِيُّ قَدْ مَلَأَ بِصَوْتِهِ الْمَكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-qumriyyu qad malaʾa bi-ṣawtihi al-makāna
sentences.l: and the turtle-dove had filled, with its voice, the place;
sentences.i: and the turtledove had filled the whole place with its voice;

sentences.t: وَالشَّحْرُورُ فِي تَغْرِيدِهِ كَأَنَّهُ إِنْسَانٌ وَالْفَاخِتُ كَأَنَّهُ شَارِبٌ نَشْوَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-shaḥrūru fī taghrīdihi ka-annahu insānun wa-al-fākhitu ka-annahu shāribun nashwānu
sentences.l: and the blackbird, in its warbling, as-if-it a human; and the ring-dove, as-if-it a drinker, drunk.
sentences.i: and the blackbird in its warbling seemed a human being, and the ringdove a tipsy drinker.
sentences.n: الفاخت is printed without the final tā' marbūṭa (usually فاختة, “ring-dove”) and is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَالْأَشْجَارُ قَدْ كَمَّلَتِ الْأَثْمَارَ مِنْ كُلِّ مَأْكُولٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ زَوْجَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ashjāru qad kammalati al-athmāra min kulli maʾkūlin wa-min kulli fākihatin zawjāni
sentences.l: And the trees had perfected the fruits — of every edible, and of every fruit a pair.
sentences.i: and the trees had brought their fruits to perfection: of every kind of food, and of every fruit, a pair.
sentences.n: I read كمّلت as “perfected” with الاثمار as its object; the print has no shadda, and “the fruits were complete” (كَمَلَتِ الْأَثْمَارُ) is possible. من كل فاكهة زوجان is the wording of Qur'an 55:52, which describes the fruits of Paradise.

sentences.t: وَالْمِشْمِسُ مَا بَيْنَ كَافُورِىٍّ وَلَوْزِيٍّ وَخُرَاسَانَ وَالْبَرْقُوقُ كَأَنَّهُ لَوْنُ الْحِسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-mishmisu mā bayna kāfūriyyin wa-lawziyyin wa-khurāsāna wa-al-barqūqu ka-annahu lawnu al-ḥisāni
sentences.l: and the apricot, (of the sorts) between camphor-ish and almond-ish and Khurāsān, and the plum, as-if-it the colour of the fair-ones.
sentences.i: and the apricots, camphor apricots and almond apricots and those of Khurāsān, and the plums, like the very hue of fair women.
sentences.n: المشمس is the print's spelling; the usual word for apricot is مشمش, so the last letter looks like a slip, and I point what is printed. Camphor-apricot and almond-apricot are named kinds of apricot; I take خراسان as a third kind, named for the province, though the print does not add the usual -ī.

sentences.t: وَالْقَرَاصِيَةُ تَقْمَعُ صُفْرَ الْأَسْنَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-qarāṣiyatu taqmaʿu ṣufra al-asnāni
sentences.l: and the sour-cherries subdue the yellows of the teeth.
sentences.i: and the sour cherries scoured the yellow from the teeth.
sentences.n: An obscure line. قمع is to beat down, check or subdue, and صفر الأسنان is “the yellow (stains) of the teeth”; I read it as the tart cherries cleaning the yellowness away, but the sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَالتِّينُ قَدْ فَرَقَ أَحْمَرَهُ وَأَبْيَضَهُ لَوْنَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-tīnu qad faraqa aḥmarahu wa-abyaḍahu lawnāni
sentences.l: and the fig had separated its red and its white — two colours.
sentences.i: and the figs had parted their red from their white, two colours.

sentences.t: وَالزَّهْرُ كَأَنَّهُ اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ وَالْوَرْدُ يَفْضَحُ بِحُمْرَتِهِ خُدُودَ الْحِسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-zahru ka-annahu al-luʾluʾu wa-al-marjānu wa-al-wardu yafḍaḥu bi-ḥumratihi khudūda al-ḥisāni
sentences.l: and the blossom, as-if-it the pearl and the coral; and the rose shames, with its redness, the cheeks of the fair-ones.
sentences.i: the blossoms were like pearls and coral, and the rose, with its redness, put to shame the cheeks of beautiful women.

sentences.t: وَالْبَنَفْسَجُ كَأَنَّهُ كِبْرِيتٌ عُلِّقَ عَلَيْهِ بِاللَّيْلِ النِّيرَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-banafsaju ka-annahu kibrītun ʿulliqa ʿalayhi bi-al-layli al-nīrānu
sentences.l: and the violet, as-if-it sulphur, on which, at night, the fires are hung.
sentences.i: and the violet like brimstone on which fires are kindled in the night.
sentences.n: The violet's blue is compared to the flame of sulphur matches; علّق عليه is “were hung (i.e. set alight) upon it”.

sentences.t: وَالْآسُ وَالْمَنْثُورُ وَالْحَدَامُ مَعَ شَقَائِقِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-āsu wa-al-manthūru wa-al-ḥadāmu maʿa shaqāʾiqi al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: and the myrtle and the gillyflower and the ḥadām, together-with the anemones (the-splits of al-Nuʿmān).
sentences.i: and the myrtle, the gillyflower and the ḥadām, with the anemones.
sentences.n: The list of flowers has no verb here. الحدام is not a word I can identify; it may be a misprint for الخزام (khuzām, a fragrant plant, perhaps lavender), but I point what is printed. شقائق النعمان is the red anemone, named, as the old etymology has it, for a king called al-Nuʿmān.

sentences.t: وَتَكَلَّلَتْ تِلْكَ الْأَوْرَاقُ بِمَدَامِعِ الْغَمَامِ وَضَحِكَ ثَغْرُ الْأُقْحُوَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-takallalat tilka al-awrāqu bi-madāmiʿi al-ghamāmi wa-ḍaḥika thaghru al-uqḥuwāni
sentences.l: and those leaves were-wreathed with the tears of the cloud, and the mouth of the chamomile laughed.
sentences.i: and those leaves were wreathed with the tears of the clouds, and the mouth of the chamomile laughed.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ النَّرْجِسُ نَاظِرًا إِلَى الْوَرْدِ بِعُيُونِ السُّودَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra al-narjisu nāẓiran ilā al-wardi bi-ʿuyūni al-sūdāni
sentences.l: and the narcissus became looking at the rose with the eyes of the blacks.
sentences.i: and the narcissus gazed at the rose with the eyes of black men.
sentences.n: The narcissus's dark centre is the eye; السودان is “the blacks”, the people of Sudan, and the image is of dark eyes in a pale face.

sentences.t: وَالْأُتْرُجُّ كَأَنَّهُ أَكْوَابٌ وَاللَّيْمُونُ كَبَنَادِقَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-utrujju ka-annahu akwābun wa-al-laymūnu ka-banādiqa min dhahabin
sentences.l: and the citron, as-if-it goblets, and the lemon like pellets of gold.
sentences.i: the citrons were like goblets and the lemons like balls of gold.
sentences.n: بنادق (sing. بندقة) is first “hazelnuts”, then “pellets, balls”; the lemons are small gold balls.

sentences.t: وَفُرِشَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِالزَّهْرِ مِنْ سَائِرِ الْأَلْوَانِ وَأَقْبَلَ الرَّبِيعُ فَأَشْرَقَ بِبَهْجَتِهِ الْمَكَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-furishati al-arḍu bi-al-zahri min sāʾiri al-alwāni wa-aqbala al-rabīʿu fa-ashraqa bi-bahjatihi al-makānu
sentences.l: and the earth was spread with the blossom, of all the colours; and spring came on, and the place shone with its splendour.
sentences.i: The earth was spread with blossoms of every hue; spring had come, and the place shone with its splendour.
sentences.n: سائر here means “all, every”, not “the rest”; the print gives its precomposed hamza-on-yā' and it is kept.

sentences.t: وَالنَّهْرُ فِي خَرِيرٍ وَالطَّيْرُ فِي هَدِيرٍ وَالرِّيحُ فِي صَفِيرٍ لِاعْتِدَالِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-nahru fī kharīrin wa-al-ṭayru fī hadīrin wa-al-rīḥu fī ṣafīrin li-iʿtidāli al-zamāni
sentences.l: and the river in murmuring, and the bird(s) in cooing, and the wind in whistling, for the temperateness of the time.
sentences.i: The river murmured, the birds cooed and the wind whistled, so mild was the season.
sentences.n: The rhymed prose (-īr) of the garden closes with this triplet. لاعتدال is printed as one word: لِـ (“for, because of”) + اعتدال.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ بِهِمَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَاعَةَ الْمُعَلَّقَةَ فَنَظَرُوا إِلَى حُسْنِ تِلْكَ الْقَاعَةِ وَتِلْكَ الشُّمُوعِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ الَّتِي فِي تِلْكَ الشَّبَابِيكِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala bihimā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu al-qāʿata al-muʿallaqata fa-naẓarū ilā ḥusni tilka al-qāʿati wa-tilka al-shumūʿi al-madhkūrati allatī fī tilka al-shabābīki
sentences.l: Then entered with them-two the shaykh Ibrāhīm the hall, the suspended; and they looked at the beauty of that hall and of those candles, the mentioned, which (were) in those windows.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm led them into the hanging hall, and they looked at the beauty of that hall and of the candles already mentioned, which stood in its windows.
sentences.n: دخل بهم is “entered with them”, that is, led them in. القاعة المعلقة is the hanging (raised) hall, an upper room; المذكورة (“the aforementioned”) points back to the earlier telling of the tale, and the print adds nothing more here.

sentences.t: فَتَذَكَّرَ نُورُالدِّينِ الْمَقَامَاتِ الَّتِي مَضَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-tadhakkara Nūru al-Dīni al-maqāmāti allatī maḍat lahu
sentences.l: and Nūr al-Dīn remembered the stations which had passed to him.
sentences.i: and Nūr al-Dīn called to mind the sojourns that had passed for him.
sentences.n: المقامات (sing. مقام) are “places of stay, sittings, stations”; I take them as his past sojourns and sessions of pleasure.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا مَقَامٌ مَلِيحٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi inna hādhā maqāmun malīḥun
sentences.l: And he said: By God, indeed this (is) a place, fine.
sentences.i: and he said, “By God, this is a fine place indeed.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا جَلَسَا فَقَدَّمَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَكْلًا فَأَكَلَا كِفَايَتَهُمَا ثُمَّ غَسَلَا أَيْدِيَهُمَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā jalasā fa-qaddama lahumā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu aklan fa-akalā kifāyatahumā thumma ghasalā aydiyahumā
sentences.l: Then, indeed they-two sat, and set-before them-two the shaykh Ibrāhīm food, and they-two ate their-sufficiency, then washed their-hands.
sentences.i: Then the two sat down, and Shaykh Ibrāhīm set food before them; they ate their fill, and washed their hands.
sentences.n: اكلا is read as the noun أَكْلًا, “food”, the object of قدّم, and not as a dual verb.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَ نُورُالدِّينِ إِلَى شُبَّاكٍ مِنْ تِلْكَ الشَّبَابِيكِ وَزَعَقَ عَلَى جَارِيَتِهِ فَأَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ فَصَارَا يَنْظُرَانِ إِلَى الْأَشْجَارِ وَقَدْ حَمَلَتْ سَائِرَ الْأَثْمَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddama Nūru al-Dīni ilā shubbākin min tilka al-shabābīki wa-zaʿaqa ʿalā jāriyatihi fa-atat ilayhi fa-ṣārā yanẓurāni ilā al-ashjāri wa-qad ḥamalat sāʾira al-athmāri
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn went forward to a window of those windows, and cried out at his slave-girl, and she came to him, and the two became looking at the trees, which had borne all the fruits.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn stepped up to one of the windows and called out to his slave-girl; she came to him, and the two of them stood looking at the trees, laden with every kind of fruit.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on شبّاك (window) and it is kept. صار followed by an imperfect verb means “began to, went on to”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ نُورُالدِّينِ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاشَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَا عِنْدَكَ شِي مِنَ الشَّرَابِ لِأَنَّ النَّاسَ يَشْرَبُونَ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَأْكُلُوا
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata Nūru al-Dīni ilā al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma wa-qāla lahu yāshaykha Ibrāhīma mā ʿindaka shī min al-sharābi li-anna al-nāsa yashrabūna baʿda an yaʾkulū
sentences.l: Then Nūr al-Dīn turned to the shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to him: O Shaykh Ibrāhīm, not with-you anything of the drink? For the people drink after that they eat.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn turned to Shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to him, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, have you nothing to drink? For people drink after they have eaten.”
sentences.n: شي is the Middle Arabic spelling of شيء (“a thing”, here “anything”), pointed shī; the question is carried by the tone alone, with no particle. ياشيخ is printed as one word. “The drink” (الشراب) is a polite way of saying wine, as the next lines show.

sentences.t: فَأَنَاهُ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بِمَاءٍ حُلْوٍ بَارِدٍ عَذْبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-anāhu al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu bi-māʾin ḥulwin bāridin ʿadhbin
sentences.l: And [he brought him] the shaykh Ibrāhīm with water, sweet, cold, fresh.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm brought him sweet, cold, fresh water.
sentences.n: The print has فاناه, which I point as printed (fa-anāhu); the sense needs فأتاه (fa-atāhu), “and he brought him”, أتى بـ being “bring”, so the ن is most likely a misprint for ت.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاشَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَا هَذَا الشَّرَابُ الَّذِي أُرِيدُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yāshaykha Ibrāhīma mā hādhā al-sharābu alladhī urīduhu
sentences.l: And he said to him: O Shaykh Ibrāhīm, not this (is) the drink which I want.
sentences.i: and he said to him, “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, this is not the drink I want.”
sentences.n: Here ما is the negative (“this is not the drink…”), not “what”; the shaykh's answer confirms it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَعَلَّكَ تُرِيدُ الْخَمْرَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu laʿallaka turīdu al-khamrata
sentences.l: And he said to him: Perhaps you want the wine.
sentences.i: and he said to him, “Perhaps it is wine you want?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni naʿam
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said to him: Yes.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said to him, “Yes.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْهَا إِنَّ لِي ثَلٰثَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً مَا فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَعَنَ شَارِبَهُ وَعَاصِرَهُ وَبَائِعَهُ وَ مُبْتَاعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aʿūdhu bi-Allāhi minhā inna lī thalāthata ʿashara sanatan mā faʿaltu dhālika li-anna al-nabiyya ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama laʿana shāribahu wa-ʿāṣirahu wa-bāʾiʿahu wa- mubtāʿahu
sentences.l: And he said: I seek-refuge in God from it! Indeed to-me (are) thirteen years (that) I have not done that, because the Prophet — God prayed upon him and greeted — cursed its drinker and its presser and its seller and its buyer.
sentences.i: Then he said, “I seek refuge in God from it! It is thirteen years since I did such a thing, for the Prophet — God bless him and give him peace — cursed the one who drinks it, the one who presses it, the one who sells it and the one who buys it.”
sentences.n: ثلثة is printed without its alif and is pointed with the dagger alif. The numeral is masculine with a feminine noun (سنة), where Classical would say ثلاث عشرة سنة; this is Middle Arabic and is kept. The print breaks the line after a stray-looking و, which I keep as a separate word before مبتاعه. The suffix -hu on all four nouns refers to the wine (الخمر being treated as masculine).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ اِسْمَعْ مِنِّي كَلِمَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni ismaʿ minnī kalimatayni
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said to him: Hear from me two words.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said to him, “Hear two words from me.”

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ قُلْ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu qul
sentences.l: He said to him: Say.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Speak.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذَا الْحِمَارُ الْمَلْعُونُ إِذَا لُعِنَ هَلْ يُصِيبُكَ مِنْ لَعْنَتِهِ شِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhā al-ḥimāru al-malʿūnu idhā luʿina hal yuṣībuka min laʿnatihi shī
sentences.l: And he said: This ass, the cursed — if he is cursed, does there befall you of his cursing anything?
sentences.i: Then he said, “This accursed donkey: if it is cursed, does any of its curse fall upon you?”
sentences.n: شي is again the Middle Arabic form of شيء (“anything”).

sentences.t: قَالَ لَا
sentences.tr: qāla lā
sentences.l: He said: No.
sentences.i: He said, “No.”

sentences.t: قَالَ خُذْ هَذَا الدِّينَارَ وَهَذَيْنِ الدِّرْهَمَيْنِ وَارْكَبْ هَذَا الْحِمَارَ وَقِفْ إِلَى بَعِيدٍ
sentences.tr: qāla khudh hādhā al-dīnāra wa-hadhayni al-dirhamayni wa-irkab hādhā al-ḥimāra wa-qif ilā baʿīdin
sentences.l: He said: Take this dinar and these-two dirhams, and ride this ass, and stand to afar.
sentences.i: He said, “Take this dinar and these two dirhams, mount this donkey, and stop some way off.”
sentences.n: The slice ends here, probably in mid-sentence: this fragment is its own unit, and the speech goes on in the lines that follow.

sentences.t: وَأَيُّ مَنْ وَجَدْتَهُ يَشْتَرِى فَنَادِ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْ لَهُ خُذْ هَذَيْنِ الدِّرْهَمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-ayyu man wajadtahu yashtarī fa-nādi ʿalayhi wa-qul lahu khudh hādhayni al-dirhamayni
sentences.l: And whichever one you find him buying, call out to him and say to him: Take these two dirhams,
sentences.i: and whomever you find buying, call out to him and say to him, “Take these two dirhams,
sentences.n: This slice opens mid-sentence: Nūr al-Dīn is still giving Shaykh Ibrāhīm his instructions, begun on the previous page, so the unit is a fragment and continues in the next one. أيّ من is “whoever”, and يشترى is spelled with ى as printed.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَرِ لِي بِهَذَا الدِّينَارِ خَمْرًا وَاحْمِلْهُ عَلَى الْحِمَارِ وَلَا تَكُنْ أَنْتَ حَمَلْتَهُ وَلَا اشْتَرَيْتَهُ وَلَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْهُ شَيْ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtari lī bi-hādhā al-dīnāri khamran wa-iḥmilhu ʿalā al-ḥimāri wa-lā takun anta ḥamaltahu wa-lā ishtaraytahu wa-lā aṣābaka minhu shay
sentences.l: and buy for me with this dinar wine, and load it upon the donkey; and do not be, you, one who carried it, nor bought it, nor did anything of it befall you.
sentences.i: and with this dinar buy me wine, and load it on the donkey; and let it not be you who carries it or buys it, so that no harm from it may touch you.”
sentences.n: This completes Nūr al-Dīn's speech begun in the previous unit. The print has شي for شيء; I vocalise it as printed, without the hamza.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَقَدْ ضَحِكَ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ وَاللَّهِ يَا وَلَدِي مَا رَأَيْتُ أَظْرَفَ مِنْكَ وَلَا أَحْلَى مِنْ كَلَامِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-qad ḍaḥika min kalāmihi wa-Allāhi yā waladī mā raʾaytu aẓrafa minka wa-lā aḥlā min kalāmika
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said — and he had laughed at his speech — By God, O my son, I have not seen one wittier than you, nor sweeter than your speech.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm, who had laughed at his words, said, “By God, my son, I have never seen a wittier fellow than you, nor one whose talk is sweeter.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فَعَلَ مَا قَالَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ فَشَكَرَهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shaykha Ibrāhīma faʿala mā qālahu Nūru al-Dīni fa-shakarahu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: Then indeed the shaykh Ibrāhīm did what Nūr al-Dīn had said, and he thanked him for that.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm did as Nūr al-Dīn had bidden him, and Nūr al-Dīn thanked him for it.
sentences.n: The print joins نورالدين into one word, and I keep it joined. The subject of فشكره, “and he thanked him”, is Nūr al-Dīn.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ نَحْنُ صِرْنَا مَحْسُوبِينَ عَلَيْكَ وَمَا عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا الْمُوَافَقَهْ تُحْضِرُ لَنَامَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu naḥnu ṣirnā maḥsūbīna ʿalayka wa-mā ʿalayka illā al-muwāfaqah tuḥḍiru lanāmā naḥtāju ilayhi
sentences.l: And he said to him: We have become reckoned upon you, and there is not upon you except the agreement: you bring to-us-what we need to it.
sentences.i: And he said to him, “We have become your charges, and nothing is asked of you but to agree: you bring us whatever we require.”
sentences.n: محسوبين عليك means “reckoned on your account”, that is, people in your care. The print spells الموافقه with ه for ة, and joins لنا and ما into لناما; both are kept as printed. تحضر is a bare present, standing where Classical Arabic would have أن تحضر, “that you bring”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَا وَلَدِي هَذَا كَرَارِي قُدَّامَكَ وَهُوَ الْحَاصِلُ الْمُعَدُّ لِأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَادْخُلْهُ وَخُذْ مِنْهُ مَا شِئْتَ فَإِنَّ فِيهِ فَوْقَ مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu yā waladī hādhā karārī quddāmaka wa-huwa al-ḥāṣilu al-muʿaddu li-amīri al-muʾminīna fa-udkhulhu wa-khudh minhu mā shiʾta fa-inna fīhi fawqa mā turīdu
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: O my son, this is my karārī, in front of you, and it is the storehouse, the prepared one, for the commander of the believers; so enter it, and take from it what you wished, for in it is above what you want.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm said, “My son, here is my place before you, and it is the storehouse kept ready for the Commander of the Faithful. Go in, and take what you please, for it holds more than you could ask.”
sentences.n: كراري is obscure. It may be a miswriting of قراري, “my abiding-place, my abode”, which suits the sense, but I vocalise the letters as printed and translate loosely as “my place”. قدامك, “in front of you”, is the colloquial form of أمامك.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ نُورُالدِّينِ الْحَاصِلَ فَرَأَى فِيهِ أَوَانِيَ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْبِلَّوْرِ مُرَصَّعَةً بِأَصْنَافِ الْجَوَاهِرِ فَأَخْرَجَهَا وَرَصَّهَا وَسَكَبَ الْخَمْرَةَ فِى الْبَوَاطِي وَالْقَنَانِي وَفَرِحَ بِمَارَأَى وَانْدَهَشَ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala Nūru al-Dīni al-ḥāṣila fa-raʾā fīhi awāniya mina al-dhahabi wa-al-fiḍḍati wa-al-billawri muraṣṣaʿatan bi-aṣnāfi al-jawāhiri fa-akhrajahā wa-raṣṣahā wa-sakaba al-khamrata fī al-bawāṭī wa-al-qanānī wa-fariḥa bi-mā raʾā wa-andahasha
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn entered the storehouse, and saw in it vessels of the gold and the silver and the crystal, studded with kinds of the jewels; and he brought them out and set them in order, and poured out the wine into the bowls and the flasks, and was glad at what he saw, and was bewildered.
sentences.i: So Nūr al-Dīn went into the storehouse and saw there vessels of gold and silver and crystal, inlaid with every kind of jewel. He brought them out and set them in order, and poured the wine into the bowls and flagons; and he rejoiced at what he saw, and was dazzled.
sentences.n: The print joins بما and راى into بماراى; I keep it as one word and read it as بِمَا رَأَى, “at what he saw”. The one mark the print gives in this unit is the shadda of ورصّها, which I keep. البواطي and القناني are the plurals of باطية, “bowl”, and قنينة, “flask”.

sentences.t: وَأَتَى لَهُمَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بِالْفَاكِهَةِ وَالْمَشْمُومِ
sentences.tr: wa-atā lahumā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu bi-al-fākihati wa-al-mashmūmi
sentences.l: And there came to the two of them the shaykh Ibrāhīm with the fruit and the smelled things.
sentences.i: Shaykh Ibrāhīm brought them fruit and fragrant flowers.
sentences.n: أتى بـ is “bring (something)”, here with لهما, “to them”. المشموم, literally “the smelled things”, is the fragrant herbs and flowers set out at a drinking party.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشَّيْخَ رَاحَ وَقَعَدَ بَعِيدً اعَنْهُمَا فَشَرِبَا وَانْبَسَطَا وَقَدْ تَحَكَّمَ مَعَهُمَا الشَّرَابُ وَاحْمَرَّتْ خُدُودُهُمَا وَتَغَازَلَتْ عُيُونُهُمَا وَأَسْبَلَتْ شُعُورُهُمَا وَتَبَدَّلَتْ أَلْوَانُهُمَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shaykha rāḥa wa-qaʿada baʿīdan ʿanhumā fa-sharibā wa-inbasaṭā wa-qad taḥakkama maʿahumā al-sharābu wa-iḥmarrat khudūduhumā wa-taghāzalat ʿuyūnuhumā wa-asbalat shuʿūruhumā wa-tabaddalat alwānuhumā
sentences.l: Then indeed the shaykh went off and sat far from the two of them; and the two drank and became expansive, and the drink had taken mastery with them, and their cheeks reddened, and their eyes flirted with each other, and their locks hung loose, and their colours changed.
sentences.i: Then the shaykh went off and sat down at a distance from them. The two drank and grew merry, and when the wine had taken hold of them, their cheeks flushed, their eyes exchanged glances, their locks fell loose, and their colours changed.
sentences.n: The print splits بعيدا عنهما into بعيد and اعنهما, so that the alif of the tanwīn stands at the head of the next word. I keep both tokens as printed, put the fatḥatān on the dāl, and read “far from them”. تغازلت عيونهما, “their eyes flirted”, means they exchanged amorous glances.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ مَانِي أَنَا قَاعِدٌ بَعِيدًا وَمَالِي لَا أَقْعُدُ عِنْدَهُمَا وَأَيُّ وَقْتٍ أَلْتَقِي فِي حَضْرَتِي مِثْلَ هَذَيْنِ الِاثْنَيْنِ اللَّذَيْنِ كَأَنَّهُمَا قَمَرَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu mānī anā qāʿidun baʿīdan wa-mālī lā aqʿudu ʿindahumā wa-ayyu waqtin altaqī fī ḥaḍratī mithla hādhayni al-ithnayni alladhayni ka-annahumā qamarāni
sentences.l: And the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: What is with me, I, sitting far away? And what is to me that I do not sit by them? And what time shall I meet, in my presence, the like of these two, the two who are as though they were two moons
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm said, “Why should I sit so far away? Why should I not sit beside them? And when shall I ever again meet in my own presence the like of these two, who are like two moons
sentences.n: The print breaks off mid-sentence here; the speech continues in the next unit, so the translation is left open. ماني is obscure; I read it as a colloquial “what ails me, that I (sit) far away?”, matching the question that follows. التقي is read as the first-person أَلْتَقِي, “I meet”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّ الشَّيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ تَقَدَّمَ وَقَعَدَ فِي طَرَفِ الْإِ يوَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma anna al-shaykha Ibrāhīma taqaddama wa-qaʿada fī ṭarafi al-ʾī wāni
sentences.l: Then that the shaykh Ibrāhīm came forward and sat in the edge-of the īwān.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm came forward and sat down at the edge of the alcove.
sentences.n: The print splits الايوان into الا يوان with a space; the two pieces are kept as printed and read together as al-īwān, the vaulted, open-fronted hall or alcove of a house. The ī is carried by the ي of the second piece.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ يَا سَيِّدِي بِحَيَاتِي عَلَيْكَ تَقَدَّمْ عِنْدَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun yā sayyidī bi-ḥayātī ʿalayka taqaddam ʿindanā
sentences.l: So he said to him, Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī: O my master, by my life upon you, come forward at-us.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to him: “My lord, by my life I beg you, come over and join us.”
sentences.n: نورالدين is printed as one word and read as the first part of the name Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī. بحياتي عليك, “by my life upon you”, is an urgent plea (“I adjure you”).

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ إِلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu ilayhimā
sentences.l: So the shaykh Ibrāhīm came forward to the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: So Shaykh Ibrāhīm drew near to the pair.

sentences.t: فَمَلَأَ نُورُالدِّينِ قَدَحًا وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَالَ لَهُ اِشْرَبْ حَتَّى تَنْظُرَ أَيْشْ طَعْمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-malaʾa Nūru al-Dīni qadaḥan wa-naẓara ilā al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma wa-qāla lahu ishrab ḥattā tanẓura ayish ṭaʿmuhu
sentences.l: So Nūr al-Dīn filled a cup and looked at the shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to him: Drink, until you see what its taste (is).
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn filled a cup, looked at Shaykh Ibrāhīm, and said to him: “Drink, and you will see what its taste is.”
sentences.n: ايش (“what?”) is the colloquial contraction of أي شيء, “which thing”; it belongs to Middle Arabic, not Classical, and recurs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَعُوذُ بِاللّٰهِ أَنَّ لِي ثَلٰثَةَ عَشَرَسَنَةً مَا فَعَلْتُ شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu aʿūdhu bi-Allāhi anna lī thalāthata ʿashara sanatan mā faʿaltu shayʾan min dhālika
sentences.l: So the shaykh Ibrāhīm said: I seek-refuge with God; that to-me (are) thirteen years (that) I have not done anything of that.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm said: “God forbid! For thirteen years I have done nothing of the kind.”
sentences.n: عشرسنة is printed as one word (ʿashara + sana, “ten … year”); it is read as the number 13 with the preceding ثلثة, whose missing alif is marked by the dagger alif. أن لي … ما فعلت is the colloquial “it is thirteen years that I have not done”.

sentences.t: فَتَغَافَلَ عَنْهُ نُورُالدِّينِ وَشَرِبَ الْقَدَحَ وَرَمَى رُوحَهُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَأَظْهَرَ أَنَّهُ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ السُّكْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-taghāfala ʿanhu Nūru al-Dīni wa-shariba al-qadaḥa wa-ramā rūḥahu ʿalā al-arḍi wa-aẓhara annahu ghalaba ʿalayhi al-sukru
sentences.l: So Nūr al-Dīn pretended-not-to-notice about-him and drank the cup and threw his soul onto the ground and showed that drunkenness had overcome him.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn paid him no heed, drank off the cup, and flung himself upon the ground, making it appear that drunkenness had overcome him.
sentences.n: رمى روحه, literally “threw his soul”, is the Middle Arabic reflexive “threw himself”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا شَيْخَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اُنْظُرْ هَذَا كَيْفَ عَمِلَ مَعِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika naẓarat ilayhi Anīsu al-Jalīsi wa-qālat lahu yā shaykha Ibrāhīma unẓur hādhā kayfa ʿamila maʿī
sentences.l: So at that, Anīs al-Jalīs looked at him and said to him: O shaykh Ibrāhīm, look at this, how he has acted with me.
sentences.i: Thereupon Anīs al-Jalīs looked at him and said: “Shaykh Ibrāhīm, see how this man has treated me!”

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهَا يَا سِتِّي مَا لَهُ
sentences.tr: qāla lahā yā sittī mā lahu
sentences.l: He said to her: O my lady, what (is) to-him?
sentences.i: He said to her: “My lady, what ails him?”

sentences.t: قَالَتْ دَائِمًا يَعْمَلُ مَعِي هَكَذَا فَيَشْرَبُ سَاعَةً وَيَنَامُ وَأَبْقَى أَنَا وَحْدِي مَا أَلْتَقِي لِي نَدِيمًا يُنَادِمُنِي عَلَى قَدَ حِي وَلَا مَنْ أُغَنِّي لَهُ عَلَى قَدَحِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat dāʾiman yaʿmalu maʿī hākadhā fa-yashrabu sāʿatan wa-yanāmu wa-abqā anā waḥdī mā altaqī lī nadīman yunādimunī ʿalā qadaḥī wa-lā man ughannī lahu ʿalā qadaḥihi
sentences.l: She said: Always he does with me thus: he drinks an hour and sleeps, and I remain, I, alone — I do not meet for-me a boon-companion who drinks-with-me over my cup, nor one for-whom I sing over his cup.
sentences.i: She said: “He always does this to me. He drinks for an hour and then sleeps, and I am left all alone, with no boon companion to drink with me over my cup, and none to whom I may sing over his.”
sentences.n: The print has قد حي with a space, evidently a slip for قدحي, “my cup”; it is kept as printed (two pieces) and read as qadaḥī. ما التقي لي is Middle Arabic for “I do not find (for myself)”; the لي is a dative of interest.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَقَدْ حَنَّتْ أَعْضَاؤُهُ وَمَالَتْ نَفْسُهُ مِنْ كَلَامِهَا إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ وَاللّٰهِ مَا هَذَا طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu wa-qad ḥannat aʿḍāʾuhu wa-mālat nafsuhu min kalāmihā ilayhā wa-qāla wa-Allāhi mā hādhā ṭayyibun
sentences.l: So the shaykh Ibrāhīm said to her — and his limbs had yearned, and his soul had inclined from her speech to her — and he said: By God, this is not good.
sentences.i: Then Shaykh Ibrāhīm said to her — for his limbs had stirred with longing, and her words had drawn his heart toward her — and he said: “By God, this is not right.”
sentences.n: The first فقال has no speech of its own: the circumstantial clause (وقد حنت …) intervenes and the words follow after the second وقال. What he finds “not good” is her being left alone to drink without company.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ مَلَأَتْ قَدَحًا وَنَظَرَتْ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ بِحَيَاتِي إِلَّا مَا أَخَذْتَهُ وَشَرِبْتَهُ وَلَا تَرُدَّهُ وَاجْبُرْ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: thumma anna al-jāriyata malaʾat qadaḥan wa-naẓarat ilā al-shaykhi Ibrāhīma wa-qālat lahu bi-ḥayātī illā mā akhadhtahu wa-sharibtahu wa-lā taruddahu wa-ijbur qalbī
sentences.l: Then that the slave-girl filled a cup and looked at the shaykh Ibrāhīm and said to him: By my life, but that you take it and drink it, and do not send it back, and mend my heart.
sentences.i: Then the girl filled a cup, looked at Shaykh Ibrāhīm, and said to him: “By my life, you must take it and drink it. Do not refuse it, but mend my heart.”
sentences.n: إلا ما + perfect is a colloquial emphatic: “you simply must (take it)”; the form is not Classical.

sentences.t: فَمَدَّ الشَّيْخُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَدَهُ وَأَخَذَ الْقَدَحَ وَشَرِبَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-madda al-shaykhu Ibrāhīmu yadahu wa-akhadha al-qadaḥa wa-sharibahu
sentences.l: So the shaykh Ibrāhīm stretched out his hand and took the cup and drank it.
sentences.i: So Shaykh Ibrāhīm stretched out his hand, took the cup, and drank it.

sentences.t: وَمَلَأَتْ لَهُ ثَانِيًا وَجَعَلَهُ عَلَى الشَّمْعَةِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي بَقِيَ لَكَ هَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-malaʾat lahu thāniyan wa-jaʿalahu ʿalā al-shamʿati wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī baqiya laka hādhā
sentences.l: And she filled for-him a second, and he put it on the candle, and she said to him: O my master, there remains for-you this (one).
sentences.i: She filled a second cup for him, and he set it down by the candle, and she said: “My lord, this one still remains for you.”
sentences.n: The verb وجعله is masculine, so the one who sets the cup down is the shaykh (she is the subject of the feminine verbs around it). على الشمعة, “on the candle”, probably means on the candlestand or beside the light; the print gives no more. ثانيا, “a second”, supplies قدحا.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَاللّٰهِ لَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَهُ يَكْفِينِي الَّذِي شَرِبْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā wa-Allāhi lā aqdiru an ashrabahu yakfīnī alladhī sharibtuhu
sentences.l: So he said to her: By God, I am not able to drink it; what I have drunk suffices me.
sentences.i: He said to her: “By God, I cannot drink it. What I have drunk is enough for me.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَاللّٰهِ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهُ فَأَخَذَ الْقَدَحَ وَشَرِبَهُ ثُمَّ أَعْطَتْهُ الثَّالِثَ فَأَخَذَهُ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَشْرَبَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-Allāhi lā budda minhu fa-akhadha al-qadaḥa wa-sharibahu thumma aʿṭathu al-thālitha fa-akhadhahu wa-arāda an yashrabahu
sentences.l: So she said to him: By God, there is no escape from it. So he took the cup and drank it; then she gave him the third, and he took it and wished to drink it.
sentences.i: She said to him: “By God, it cannot be avoided.” So he took the cup and drank it, and she gave him the third, which he took and was about to drink.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِنُورِالدِّينِ هَمَّ وَقَعَدَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-Nūri al-Dīni hamma wa-qaʿada ʿalā ḥaylihi
sentences.l: And behold, Nūr al-Dīn stirred and sat on his strength.
sentences.i: When lo, Nūr al-Dīn stirred and sat up of his own strength.
sentences.n: وإذا بـ marks only what suddenly appears. حيله is read as ḥaylihi, “his strength, his own power”; the sense is that he sat up by himself, shaking off his pretended stupor, but the phrase is obscure and the reading is a best guess.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted tale unspoken.
sentences.n: The standard closing formula, in rhyme (ṣabāḥ / mubāḥ). The print splits the name into شهر زاد, two pieces, kept as printed.
